cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village called Aṭṭaluvuḍu situated in the midst of the villages Karakuṇḍa, Kamsāryya, Velkuṇḍukuriki, Maṇivardda and Pallaveñcha, in Talupāka-viṣaya to the asceitics of Ārya-bhikṣu-samgha belonging to the 18 sections (nikāya) who had come from four directions and resided at the famous mahāvihāra on the eastern skirts of Guṇapāśapura hill for their clothing, food, beds, seats and medical treatment by the king from his provincial capital Nandivardhana. Pañchanadīśvara temple. On the south wall, central shrine.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of ten kaļañju of gold by Teļļāru-ēriņda Nandippōttaraiyar to burn a perpetual lamp to the deity Mahādēva of Tiruvaiyāru. cells.remarks: Shājahānpūr. Composed by Abr. Records the history and political career of the family of Dīwān ʿAbbās Khān, son of Yāsīn Khān, son of Ismāʿīl Khān, of the Dilāzāk Karrānī tribe (of the Afghāns). Also records that Dīwān ʿAbbās Khān, migrated from his native place Mātūrī or Shivgī, District Mardān, to India in the ending years of the reign of Jahāngīr. During the time of migration, he stayed in the village Surāī Ṣāliḥ, a stronghold of the Dilāzāks. Later he made his stay in Jalandhar where his brother Sayyid Muḥammad Khān had settled permanently. Afterwards, he halted for some time at Khūrja and Basai in Bulandshahr District. Ultimately, in the early years of Shājahān’s period, about 1632 A.D. he laid the foundation of Shājahānpūr. Records the history and political career of the family of Dīwān ʿAbbās Khān, son of Yāsīn Khān, son of Ismāʿīl Khān, of the Dilāzāk Karrānī tribe (of the Afghāns). Also records that Dīwān ʿAbbās Khān, migrated from his native place Mātūrī or Shivgī, District Mardān, to India in the ending years of the reign of Jahāngīr. During the time of migration, he stayed in the village Surāī Ṣāliḥ, a stronghold of the Dilāzāks. Later he made his stay in Jalandhar where his brother Sayyid Muḥammad Khān had settled permanently. Afterwards, he halted for some time at Khūrja and Basai in Bulandshahr District. Ultimately, in the early years of Shājahān’s period, about 1632 A.D. he laid the foundation of Shājahānpūr.
